extracted.intended_audience: public relations students and crisis communication practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style analysis of crisis communication strategies, using the Johnson & Johnson Tylenol cyanide tampering incident to illustrate principles for organizational response, media relations, and remediation/rectification. Intended to teach how to manage public safety, reputation, and prevention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public safety as top priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership's first strategy guidance was 'How do we protect the people?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make public safety the organization's number one concern in communications and decision-making during a crisis; prioritize actions that minimize harm even at significant cost to the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize saving the product/brand after safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership's second strategy guidance was 'How do we save this product?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After ensuring public safety, take measures to regain control of the product/brand through transparent actions, remediation, and rectification to restore consumer trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid, decisive action (including full product withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson withdrew all Tylenol capsules nationally, stopping production and advertising and removing products from shelves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take immediate, decisive remedial steps (e.g., product withdrawal) even when the probability of further contamination is low; decisive action demonstrates unwillingness to risk public safety and can reframe public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use transparent, open communications with the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson issued a national alert telling the public not to use Tylenol and communicated that consumers should not resume use until extent of tampering was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate clearly and openly through the media to warn the public and explain the organization's stance; openness helps disseminate warnings and builds trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish consumer and media information channels (hotlines, toll-free lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1-800 hotline for consumers and a toll-free line for news organizations with pre-taped daily messages were established in the first week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up dedicated communication channels quickly to handle inquiries and provide consistent, updated information to both consumers and news organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership visibility and direct spokespersoning
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO (Jim Burke) held press conferences, appeared on national TV (60 Minutes, Donahue), and used satellite feeds to make messages national.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure senior leadership is visible, gives personal messages, and appears in media to convey command, empathy, and credibility; use live feeds to reach broad audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a focused crisis strategy team with clear priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson formed a seven-member strategy team with explicit guidance from the chairman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly convene a small strategy team with clear, prioritized objectives to coordinate response decisions and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation: provide assistance and compensation to victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson provided victims' families counseling and financial assistance even though the company was not responsible for the tampering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer remediation to affected parties (counseling, financial assistance) to help victims and demonstrate organizational concern; remediation can lessen negative public feelings even when not at fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification: take actions to prevent recurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rectification involves taking action to prevent recurrence—example: development of triple sealed packaging and new random inspection procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement tangible, preventive measures (product redesign, new inspection protocols) quickly to reduce future risk and signal commitment to safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sympathy and forgiveness strategies to win public support
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson employed Forgiveness and Sympathy strategies: Sympathy portrays the organization as an unfair victim, and Forgiveness seeks to win forgiveness from publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the crisis is caused by external actors, portray the organization empathetically as a victim and seek public forgiveness through actions and communication that elicit support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify the crisis to guide attribution and response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tylenol case is classified as Terrorism (product tampering); Coombs defines terrorism as intentional external actions designed to harm the organization directly or indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify crisis category (terrorism/product tampering, faux pas, accident, transgression) to determine loci of responsibility, controllability, and the most appropriate communication strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate the media may have information first; monitor and respond
rubrics_metrics.description: The media will often be the first on the scene and have information about the crisis before the organization does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain active media monitoring and be prepared to respond rapidly; acknowledge gaps in knowledge honestly and provide updates as facts are verified to avoid being out-led by reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain proactive media relations pre-crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the crisis, J&J had not actively sought press coverage; lack of positive media relationships forced them to respond in an advertising-like manner and raised criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate positive media relationships before a crisis to ensure credibility and avoid being perceived as insincere when responding; proactive public affairs programs improve trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple channels (PR, paid ads, press conferences, live feeds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson & Johnson used PR, paid advertising, press conferences, and live satellite feeds to disseminate messages nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy a mix of earned and paid media and in-person or live channels to reach diverse publics and ensure consistent messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be authentic—avoid communications that appear 'slick' or sales-like
rubrics_metrics.description: J&J received criticism for 'slick sales-like response ads' and was seen as less genuine until personal CEO messages overcame that problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure response communications are perceived as genuine and empathetic; personal leadership communications can counterbalance or correct perceptions of insincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept short-term financial cost to preserve long-term reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: By withdrawing all Tylenol despite the high cost, J&J demonstrated they would not risk public safety—even at millions of dollars in losses—and were later viewed sympathetically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to take actions that incur immediate financial loss if they protect public safety and long-term brand viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act quickly to establish industry-leading safety measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Tylenol became the first product in the industry to use new tamper-resistant packaging just 6 months after the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Move rapidly to implement visible, industry-leading fixes that set new safety standards and restore consumer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case learnings to inform future crisis strategies and scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tylenol case formed the basis for crisis communication strategies (Berg's suffering strategy, Benoit's rectification strategies) in scholarly work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document actions and outcomes, and translate practical lessons into formal strategies and training to improve future preparedness and response.
